scenes.subtitle: Fmaj7, the friendly F.
lines: Welcome.
This lesson teaches Fmaj7 — the friendly F — part of level 7.
We'll play it clearly, with no tricks.

scenes.heading: Fmaj7: the friendly F
lines: The full F chord is a barre chord that most beginners find very hard.
Fmaj7 is a friendly substitute: finger 3 on string 4 at fret 3, finger 2 on string 3 at fret 2, finger 1 on string 2 at fret 1, and string 1 open.
Strum from string 4.
Play it slowly at first, then let your fingers find the rhythm.
You're doing great — every chord you learn brings you closer to playing the songs you love.
Keep going, you've got this!
Let's learn F major 7.
It's a warm, jazzy chord that adds color to your playing.
Finger 1 goes on string 2, fret 1.
Finger 2 goes on string 3, fret 2.
Finger 3 goes on string 4, fret 3.
Don't play strings 6 and 5.
Here's how it sounds: strummed, then string by string.
scenes.tip: Keep finger 1 curved so the open high E rings: that open string is what makes it a major 7.

lines: Let's practice changing between C major and F major 7.
Move your fingers smoothly from one shape to the next, and you'll get the hang of it in no time.
Let's put it all together.
Play Fmaj7, and the app will listen through the microphone — ready when you are.
